contribution: Experimental and behavioral economics, particularly how social preferences such as fairness, reciprocity and inequity aversion, and bounded rationality shape strategic and economic behavior
rationale: This is an uncertain guess. Recent prizes went to institutions (2024) and innovation-driven growth (2025), so the committee may turn to a micro field. Fehr is a perennial favorite in citation-based forecasts, and his work on social preferences, along with Camerer's behavioral game theory and Rabin's models of fairness and reference dependence, form a coherent body of work. Thaler's 2017 prize did not cover this strand. Plausible alternatives include microeconometrics (Blundell, Manski), macroeconomics (Blanchard, Galí) and public finance (Saez).
